props.title: Why a schema enters as types, travels as text, and returns as types

beats.narration_text: TypeScript types vanish at runtime and Claude only emits plain text, yet `client.messages.parse()` hands back a fully typed object in the exact shape you declared — with no validation code from you.

The SDK encodes the Zod schema to a JSON Schema constraint outbound, Claude returns a conformant JSON string, then the SDK validates that string back through the SAME in-memory Zod object — recovering both runtime value and static type. The schema is touched at both ends of the arc.
beats.visual: A ring-shaped pipeline: Zod schema → JSON Schema (out) → JSON string (back) → Zod `.parse()` → typed object, same node at both ends.
beats.scaffold_note: the resolving mechanism; orbits the visual object

beats.narration_text: `z.object({primes: z.array(z.number())})` → JSON Schema in the request → Claude returns `{"primes":[2,3,5]}` → Zod validates → caller gets `{primes:[2,3,5]}` typed `number[]`.

The SDK encodes the Zod schema to a JSON Schema constraint outbound, Claude returns a conformant JSON string, then the SDK validates that string back through the SAME in-memory Zod object — recovering both runtime value and static type. The schema is touched at both ends of the arc.

Your turn. Paste this: you use zodOutputFormat and read parsed_output as a typed object but you want to understand what's actually happening on the wire between your code and the API. Ask Claude to show you the transformation — what format the Zod schema becomes when sent to the API, what format the response comes back in, and why parse is necessary rather than just reading the content field directly.
